I am tired of answering the same questions over and over again from  anti-Israel folks, so here is my position on the topic of relative threats and hierarchy of priorities for Christians when it comes to international relations.

I live in CANADA and my area of influence is here. Nearly 600 Churches have been destroyed in recent years, Christians are persecuted for not bowing to progressive ideology, and the Muslim supremacists on our streets are a threat to ALL Canadians. Believe me, my hands are already full here.

Be that as it may, let's have a look at overseas threats to Christians, since many Christians seem to be low information on relative threats.

Israel does not intentionally target Christians. Deaths of Christians in the war against Hamas are because of Hamas.

Muslim supremacists on the other hand, DO target Christians and have done so for 1400 years.

They have slaughtered approximately 50,000 Christians-citizens of those countries-in the past 20 years alone.

Here is a breakdown which is by no means exhaustive:

a) Muslim supremacists have killed over 30,000 Christians in Nigeria alone since 2005. Boko Haram, Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), Fulani extremists carried out many of the attacks.

b) Thousands have been killed in Iraq. The Christian population has shrunk from ~1.5 million in 2003 to <200,000 in 2024

c) Hundreds in Egypt. Churches get bombed. Funerals are attacked. Christian girls are kidnapped, forcibly converted, and married off to Muslims.

d) Indonesia, Somalia, Libya, Kenya, Afghanistan, Philippines account for hundreds of deaths. From jihadist groups Al-Shabaab, Abu Sayyaf, Taliban, among others.

d) Hundreds have been murdered in Pakistan. Christians get lynched.

e) Syria. Thousands by ISIS. There will be more with the new regime.

g) Gaza. Rami Khader Ayyad was kidnapped, tortured, and murdered. Repeated arson attacks of Christian book stores and targeted shootings of Christians, during factional clashes was normal in Gaza. The population decreased by 2/3 due to such threats and intimidation.

So by all means spend your time focused on the accidental deaths of Christians during war time in Gaza, but I am going to focus on tangible threats in my own backyard as well as the millions of Christians who are being persecuted by Muslim supremacist neighbours and regimes in their own countries.

🇺🇸 U.S. Market Summary | Tuesday, July 22, 2025

The U.S. stock market ended mixed today.

The S&P 500 hit another all-time high despite weakness in tech stocks, as funds rotated into defensive sectors such as healthcare and materials. Over 400 stocks in the S&P 500 finished higher, although the ‘Magnificent 7’ index declined for the first time in nine sessions.

However, corporate earnings showed mixed results:
•Lockheed Martin plunged 11% after reporting Q2 revenue below expectations.
•General Motors (GM) dropped 8.1% after revealing an $1.1 billion hit from tariffs, intensifying market concerns about Trump’s trade policies.

The semiconductor sector also remained under pressure.
Investor sentiment weakened following a Wall Street Journal report that SoftBank and OpenAI’s $500 billion AI initiative, Project Stargate, was facing difficulties.
After hours, Texas Instruments released disappointing guidance, adding to the sector’s headwinds.

Still, the overall earnings season remains strong.
According to FactSet, 85% of S&P 500 companies that have reported so far have beaten expectations.
Investors are now closely watching for forward guidance on macroeconomic risks, tariff impacts, and AI-related demand.

⸻

🌐 Trade Uncertainty & Geopolitics
•President Trump announced a finalized trade agreement with the Philippines, while Canada’s Prime Minister stated they are working to stabilize relations with the U.S.
•Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed a 3rd round of trade talks with China in Stockholm next week to discuss a tariff ceasefire extension.
•Bessent also stated there would be no changes in Fed Chair Powell’s position, though Trump continues to push for a 3 percentage point rate cut.

⸻

📊 Market Commentary
•Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi (UBS Global):
“The threat to Fed independence and lingering geopolitical risk could increase market volatility as we approach the August 1 tariff deadline.”
•Kevin Gordon (Charles Schwab):
“The recent modest rally suggests valuations may be stretched.”

Higher forest cover can help reduce the volume of floodwater generated in a watershed by 27% to 47% during the three wettest months of the year compared to a ‘No Forest’ cover simulation in the UMRBPL.”

[Note: The Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape currently only has ~25% forest cover based on available data, despite being protected by law since 1904.]
